title: finding(components): the icon seam's tokeniser never splits the letter-to-digit boundary, so 147 canonical PascalCase lucide names resolve nowhere in the platform
body:
Filed by the `os-dev` seat working objectui#7472 (session `session_01FhBNJcLRZLe8M87VcUgpKr`), as an out-of-scope finding measured while wiring `packages/cli`'s generated layout to the seam. Unlabelled: routing and priority belong to triage, and this seat does not produce a `domain:` label.

Not fixed in objectui#7472's PR, deliberately — that card's fence is explicit that the seam's contract is not to be re-opened, and widening the tokeniser changes behaviour for every censused resolver at once, not just the one call site that card moves.

## The finding

`packages/components/src/lib/lazy-icon.tsx`'s `toKebabIconName` is the platform's single tokeniser since objectui#5935. It splits two boundaries:

```
.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g, '$1-$2')      // lower-or-digit  ->  Upper
.replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g, '$1-$2')   // acronym run     ->  Word
```

Neither splits **letter to digit**. So `Building2` tokenises to `building2`, and lucide's canonical key is `building-2`. The name is rejected and `getLazyIcon` degrades to the `Database` fallback.

`Building2` is not an obscure spelling: it is the PascalCase component `lucide-react` exports, the spelling an author copies out of lucide's own site, and the spelling that worked in a generated CLI app until objectui#7472.

## Measurement

Measured on `origin/main` at `9ba7e9c3a2`, against `lucide-react@1.35.0` as resolved from `packages/components` in this workspace. Populations named in words:

| population | count |
|:--|--:|
| `lucide-react` namespace export keys (every spelling the library exports) | 6,110 |
| of those, component-valued | 6,109 |
| canonical kebab icon names (`iconNames` from `lucide-react/dynamic.mjs`) — what the seam accepts | 2,039 |
| component keys that DO survive `toKebabIconName` | 1,882 |
| component keys that do NOT | 4,227 |

Splitting the 4,227 by shape:

| shape | count | verdict |
|:--|--:|:--|
| `*Icon` suffix aliases (`HouseIcon`) | 2,037 | correctly rejected — alias, not a canonical key |
| `Lucide*` prefix aliases (`LucideHouse`) | 2,036 | correctly rejected — same |
| neither alias shape | 154 | **the finding** |

Of those 154, **147 are recovered by adding a letter-to-digit split and nothing else**: `ArrowDown01`, `Axis3D`, `BarChart2`, `BarChart3`, `BarChart4`, `BookUp2`, `Building2`, `Calendar1`, `CalendarCheck2`, `CheckCircle2`, `CircleSlash2`, `Clock1`, and 135 more.

The remaining 7 are `Grid2x2`, `Grid2x2Check`, `Grid2x2Plus`, `Grid2x2X`, `Grid3x2`, `Grid3x3` — where the digit-letter-digit run needs more than one rule — plus `useLucideContext`, which is a hook and correctly rejected.

Reproduce (run from `packages/components` so the specifiers resolve):

```
node --input-type=module -e "
import * as L from 'lucide-react';
import { iconNames } from 'lucide-react/dynamic.mjs';
const k = (n) => n.includes('-') ? n.toLowerCase()
  : n.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g,'\$1-\$2').replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g,'\$1-\$2').toLowerCase();
const kd = (n) => n.includes('-') ? n.toLowerCase()
  : n.replace(/([a-z0-9])([A-Z])/g,'\$1-\$2').replace(/([A-Z]+)([A-Z][a-z])/g,'\$1-\$2').replace(/([A-Za-z])([0-9])/g,'\$1-\$2').toLowerCase();
const v = new Set(iconNames);
const keys = Object.keys(L).filter((x) => x !== 'icons');
const lost = keys.filter((x) => !v.has(k(x)));
const other = lost.filter((x) => !/Icon\$/.test(x) && !/^Lucide/.test(x));
console.log('namespace keys', keys.length, '| canonical names', v.size);
console.log('non-alias keys the tokeniser drops', other.length);
console.log('recovered by a digit-boundary split', other.filter((x) => v.has(kd(x))).length);
console.log('CONTROL, must be true:', v.has(k('House')), v.has(kd('Home')));
"
```

## Why no gate catches it

`scripts/check-lucide-icon-record-names.mjs` judges **authored/declared names that reach a resolver** against the live `icons` keys. Its reading on `9ba7e9c3a2` is

```
OK  lucide icon names: 184 authored/declared names reaching 1 record-reading resolver are live `icons` keys
```

Green, and correctly so: nothing in the tree currently authors a digit-suffixed name. The gate is a census of what IS authored, not of what the tokeniser CAN accept, so this gap is latent rather than live. It becomes live the first time an author copies `Building2` off lucide's site.

## Severity, stated honestly

No user-visible failure today — the same shape as objectui#7472 itself. What an author gets is the `Database` fallback rather than an error, so the symptom is a wrong glyph, not a crash or a blank.

## Not in this card

- ⛔ Widening `DECLARED_RECORD_READERS` or the gate's discovery predicate. Unrelated, and objectui#7472 already ruled that direction out for its own site.
- The 7 `Grid2x2`-shaped names. A single letter-to-digit rule does not fix them and they may not be worth a rule of their own; whoever takes this should decide that deliberately rather than inherit it.
- Whether the fix belongs in the tokeniser or in an explicit alias table. Both reach the 147; a tokeniser rule is smaller, an alias table is auditable. That is a design call for the taker.

Refs: objectui#5935 (the seam and its ruling) · objectui#7472 (where this was measured) · objectui#7830 (the adjacent, closed finding about identifiers imported as components that are not `icons` keys).
